Contract status

FHT contract status
StatusDraft — not released. This is the development contract only: no shared release, no release tag, no fixed alias and no DOI exists for it, and no released tool validates it.
Versions this schema accepts1.0. A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state any earlier minor of the same major, and holds each of them to that minor: what a later minor allows is invalid in an earlier one.
What it describesFHT is the proposed FAIR-bioHeaders header for a reference transcriptome FASTA file. In the draft it uses the same ;~ header block and the same SHA-512/256 checksum rules as the rest of the family, and records how the transcript set was constructed, which sample and library context was supplied, and which reviewed family parent it derives from.
What it does not coverFHT describes the transcript set as a resource. It does not describe per-record expression, does not accept an unknown construction history, and does not certify that any transcript is complete or experimentally expressed.

Serializations with verified support

  • The development repository ships synthetic FASTA examples with a ;~ header block, one per construction type, plus JSON and YAML forms of one header. Their names, statistics and sequence bytes are invented; the taxon and ontology identifiers are real.
  • No JSON-LD or HTML microdata form exists for FHT in the draft.
  • The draft accepts x- extension keys at the top level, following rule R15.

Tools that implement this contract

  • No released tool supports FHT. fair-bioheaders 0.11.0 (the current PyPI release, 2026-11-14) bundles released schemas for FHR, FHP and FHGFF3 only; its FHT copy is a pinned draft. By default bioheaders assess recognises the FHT development URL and reports the header as not assessed with reason unsupported-header-type, and validate, combine, verify and verify-links read an FHT citation as FHR (rule V5), so no command validates, writes, checksums or parent-checks an FHT file. 0.11.0 adds an opt-in preview of that behaviour: with BIOHEADERS_EXPERIMENTAL_FHT=1 those commands select the bundled draft contract and report ExperimentalDraftWarning — a recorded derivedFrom parent then reports matched, not matched or not checked. The lane is preparation for publication, not support — FHT has no release, no w3id alias and no registry entry — and assess reports FHT as not assessed with the gate open or closed (checked 2026-11-14). Toolkit support is FHT-Specification#9.
  • The browser table builder on this site has no FHT form: it enables the released FHR, FHP and FHGFF3 contracts only, and FHT stays disabled until a contract is released (fair-bioheaders.github.io#15).
  • Field decisions, the model and the generated development schema live in FHT-Specification; shared publication is coordinated through FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#107.

Schema location

  • Development schema only, and it moves with main: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHT-Specification/main/fht.json. Read it as a review input, not a citable release.
  • No w3id alias, release-tag URL or DOI exists for this type, so none is offered. Release work is tracked in [FHT-Specification#10](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHT-Specification/issues/10) and shared publication in [FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#107](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/issues/107).
  • Model source: [FHT-Specification](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHT-Specification) on main, pinned here at commit 720e7f32d9. The JSON Schema is generated from the LinkML model and is never hand-edited.
  • Schema-version registry: schemas/versions.json and docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md.

Release history

The shared version registry has no entry for this type: nothing has been released, so there is no schemaVersion history to cite.

Field reference

Every field of the contract appears here, including the fields and objects inherited from the shared core: nothing is left out because another type also uses it. Required means the key must be present; when present, requires lists the members that become mandatory once you supply an optional object. Constraints are reproduced verbatim from the schema, so a pattern you see here is the pattern the validator matches. Examples are the values stated by the released example records, which are synthetic, or an illustrative value where no example reaches the field.

Top-level fields

Every field of the proposed FHT 1.0 record. The record is a closed object: an unknown top-level key is invalid, apart from the x- extension fields listed last. Nine fields are required: schema, schemaVersion, transcriptome, assemblyType, taxon, version, metadataAuthor, dateCreated and checksum.

assemblyTypeRequiredstring
  • one of: de novo | genome-guided | annotation-derived

Construction case for the whole described transcript set

de novo: reads reconstructed with no reference genome constructing or grouping the assembly; genome-guided: read evidence plus a reference constructed models or grouped reads; annotation-derived: sequences extracted from existing annotation coordinates and the matching genome.

It describes construction, not quality or deposit class. There is deliberately no mixed or unknown value: a composite or uncertain history leaves the record incomplete until it is reviewed.

Genome guidance alone never justifies a transcribedFrom parent link.

completenessOptionalobject (Completeness)when present, requires lineageDataset, completeSingle, completeDuplicated, fragmented, missing, totalmembers listed belownone stated

Optional BUSCO completeness counts from the actual run. lineageDataset must match the pinned shared pattern (a name ending in _odb plus digits, such as hymenoptera_odb10), so dotted dataset versions such as hymenoptera_odb12.2 are rejected. Do not rename a dotted lineage to pass the pattern; omit completeness and keep the measured lineage and counts in documentation until shared #170 decides dotted lineage support.

Counts from an actual BUSCO run only; a legacy free-text completeness string is never converted into counts. Counts describe ortholog groups, not transcripts or genes.

The shared lineage pattern allows _odb plus digits, so a dotted dataset version such as hymenoptera_odb12.2 cannot be represented. Keep the measured lineage and counts in documentation rather than renaming it (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#170).

derivedFromOptionalarray of DerivedFrom objectsarray of DerivedFrom objects, 1 or morewhen present, requires headerType, checksum, relationshipmembers listed belownone stated

Reviewed FAIR-bioHeaders parent-file relationships only. This contract permits an FHT filteredFrom parent or an FHR transcribedFrom parent when the transcript bases were extracted from that genome; genome guidance alone never justifies transcribedFrom. Annotation coordinates and other sources stay in relatedLink/documentation until the shared relationship vocabulary is decided (#54). The shared DerivedFrom object requires the parent's FHR-family checksum; an accession alone is not a verified family link.

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

Reviewed family parents only, and only two pairs are permitted by both the draft schema and model: FHT + filteredFrom (a subset or filtered copy of another FHT file) and FHR + transcribedFrom (transcript bases actually extracted from that genome).

FHP parents and every other headerType/relationship pairing are rejected by the schema's anyOf constraint. Structural validity cannot establish that the asserted derivation is factually true; review its evidence before publishing.

At least one item is required when the array is present, and each item must carry the parent's FHR-family checksum — an accession alone is not a verified family link.

The pattern admits the FHT-Specification raw-main URL, a future raw-tag URL and a future persistent alias on the project's w3id prefix — but only the raw-main form exists today. No alias has been minted and no release tag has been cut, so a draft record cites the development URL.

The released toolkit recognises the FHT URL and reports it as not assessed (unsupported-header-type): the pattern is not support.

strandednessOptionalstring
  • one of: unstranded | forward | reverse

Supplied library strandedness under the FHT read/read-1 convention: forward means the single read or read 1 is sense relative to the originating transcript, reverse means antisense. Unknown or mixed protocols are omitted, never defaulted to unstranded.

FHT's own normalization — unstranded, forward or reverse — where forward means the single read or read 1 is sense relative to the originating transcript.

It is not an ENA enum, not genomic plus/minus orientation, and not the orientation of exported transcript sequences. Unknown or mixed protocols are omitted, never defaulted to unstranded.

x-<name>Optionalany JSON valuesingle value or array, at any depth
  • pattern: ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$

Extension field (rule R15): a top-level key the standard does not define, holding any value the producer needs.

Accepted by the draft contract, mirroring FHR 2.1 and FHP/FHGFF3 1.1. Every other unknown key is still rejected, nested objects stay closed, and an extension never replaces a standard field.

JSON-LD and HTML forms would omit extension fields; FHT has neither form.

Because FHT is unreleased, an extension key in a draft record is a compatibility risk with no fixed contract to return to — prefer documentation until the contract is released.

sample[] — supplied biological sample context

One entry per biological source. Pooled material is repeated entries, each with only the values actually known for that source.

  • The object is closed: an unknown key inside it is invalid, and so is an x- extension key at this level (rule R15).
  • One member must be supplied: tissue, tissueIdentifier, developmentalStage, condition, strain.
  • At least one member must be present in every entry; sample: [{}] is invalid.

Rules beyond a single field

FHT conditional and object-level rules, read from the schema bytes.
RuleWhat the contract requires
No key may contain a line feedpropertyNames rejects any key containing a line feed, so a YAML continuation artefact cannot pass as part of a field name.
The record is a closed objectadditionalProperties: false — any other unknown top-level key is invalid, and every nested object is closed in the same way. Legacy draft keys that were dropped (masking, license, the free-text completeness string) are therefore rejected, not tolerated.
Extension fields (rule R15)Top-level keys matching ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ are accepted by the draft contract, following rule R15 of the shared FORMAT.md. There is no version gate: FHT 1.0 is the only proposed minor, so the draft has no earlier contract to protect.

What the schema cannot say

The contract is more than its JSON Schema. These requirements are normative for a conforming record, and a validator that cannot check them must say so:

  • This page documents a draft. Nothing here is adopted guidance, and the field set can still change before release.
  • The JSON Schema enforces the permitted derivedFrom pairs (FHT + filteredFrom, FHR + transcribedFrom), but cannot establish whether the asserted parent relationship is factually true.
  • The shared BUSCO lineage pattern cannot express a dotted dataset version such as hymenoptera_odb12.2 (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#170).
  • The legacy fht-v0.1.json draft schema, its examples and the retired FHT-File-Converter are historical review inputs, not FHT 1.0 and not current support. masking and license are gone; MD5 checksums are invalid.
